player.speaker: Revolutionary Delegate
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Anna Keller
line.reaction-briliant.text: The stationmaster has put two government troop trains in the sidings. He heard about your coastal columns and decided to help. Keep your men nearby; he may need more than our thanks.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Anna Keller
line.reaction-tactical.text: The police are distributing a handbill about your losses on the coast. It's given the men guarding the telegraph room some courage. Our railwaymen want to hear your account before they act.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Anna Keller
line.reaction-victory.text: The northern council seals got your train through. Here you'll have to deal with the police and municipal offices. They still have orders from the old authorities and mean to carry them out.
line.callback-region-secured.speaker: Anna Keller
line.callback-region-secured.text: Four telegrams, four council seals: Norden, Aurich, Emden, Oldenburg. The railwaymen carry your despatches free of charge now and leave the government's sacks on the platform.
line.callback-region-partial.speaker: Anna Keller
line.callback-region-partial.text: This handbill says your coastal rising has already been stopped. It was printed in one of the towns your columns never reached, and the police are passing copies through the barracks.
line.callback-doctrine-rapid.speaker: Anna Keller
line.callback-doctrine-rapid.text: Your men haven't slept under a roof since Kiel. I can ask the railway crews to move them again, but tell me how many can manage another march when they get off.
line.callback-doctrine-methodical.text: You brought your column in fed and armed. The police used the delay to fortify the telegraph room. The barracks are offering hot meals to soldiers who stay out of this. We need to speak to them soon.
line.frankfurt-platform.speaker: Anna Keller
line.frankfurt-platform.text: Keep your men off the tracks. The crews have banked the fires, and they're waiting for our signal. The police can see soldiers pulling off their imperial cockades. So far, they haven't moved.
line.keller-opening.speaker: Anna Keller
line.keller-opening.text: The railwaymen will stop troop trains for you. They need guards at the stations, though. If the police take them back, the delegates will be arrested before we can warn them.
line.weber-question.speaker: Otto Weber
line.weber-question.text: One company has elected delegates. The next has locked its armoury. They'll accept your field orders until we have a Frankfurt council, but we can't wait long. Do we call the assembly first or take the communications?
line.weber-question.choice.take-infrastr: Take the station, bridges, post and telegraph. Stop the authorities bringing troops into Frankfurt while we organise the council.
Gain a prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo the two additional worker battalions.
line.weber-question.choice.declare-counc: Call the assembly first. Let the soldiers see who is asking for their support before we go to the barracks.
Raise two worker battalions and earn their later political support, but pay prestige and forgo core-wide experience.
line.adler-infrastructure.speaker: Dr. Jakob Adler
line.adler-infrastructure.role: Municipal Doctor and Relief Liaison — Fictional Composite
line.adler-infrastructure.text: These keys open the municipal flour stores. I will hand them to an elected council, not to the first armed man at the door. Put one of my clerks beside every guard and I will keep bread carts moving while you take the switchboards.
line.keller-infrastructure-answer.text: Keep the keys, Doctor. Send your clerks to meet our delegates at the stores. I'll have the guards told who may authorise the bread carts.
line.keller-assembly.speaker: Anna Keller
line.keller-assembly.text: The unions can fill the square before noon, and soldiers who will not follow a secret committee may follow a council elected in front of them. But while the speeches are being made, trusted crews must close the stations to hostile troop movements.
line.weber-assembly-objection.speaker: Otto Weber
line.weber-assembly-objection.text: There's already a troop train signalled from the west. Hold your vote, but let the railway crews stop that train now. They can't wait for the result.
line.adler-assembly.speaker: Dr. Jakob Adler
line.adler-assembly.role: Municipal Doctor and Relief Liaison — Fictional Composite
line.adler-assembly.text: Then tell the assembly I have flour for two days and a clinic short of bandages. I need someone authorised to arrange tomorrow's deliveries before they leave the square.
line.loyalist-warning.speaker: Loyalist District Command
line.loyalist-warning.text: All railway, postal and municipal facilities are to remain under lawful authority. Armed councils will be dispersed and military property recovered.
line.weber-final.speaker: Otto Weber
line.weber-final.text: I'll go to the companies. Those that elect delegates can keep their weapons under the council; those that resist will be disarmed. Anna, keep the line east open. Berlin needs to hear what we decide.
